newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Court rules against prosecuting Yugoslav general.
newsitem.headline: Court rules against prosecuting Yugoslav general.

text.p: A Ljubljana court said on Monday it had decided against prosecuting a former Yugoslav general who fought against Slovene troops in a brief war of independence from federal Yugoslavia in 1991.
The court said it had dismissed charges that General Milan Aksentijevic had cooperated with enemy forces because he had joined the Yugoslav federal army before hostilities began.
Aksentijevic arrived in Slovenia from Belgrade in July to visit his family, and was first brought before Ljubljana's district court on July 18.
He was born in Kragujevac in Serbia in 1935 and used to be a member of the Slovenian parliament before independence was declared on June 25, 1991.
He left the country with the Yugoslav army after the brief war but was not allowed to return until last year. His Slovenian wife and grown-up children live in Slovenia.
Aksentijevic had applied for permission to remain in Slovenia but this was turned down by the Interior Ministry. His appeal will be considered by the end of October, the ministry said.
